finding.claim: The /settings/email POST endpoint uses @login_optional instead of @login_required, so unauthenticated requests reach the email-change operation. g.uid is None for anonymous callers, and set_email is called with uid=None. The sibling /settings/password endpoint correctly uses @login_required, which shows the intent. If set_email is implemented with a lookup like WHERE id = uid, the anonymous caller could change the email on a null or unmatched account. With ORM filters that treat None specially, the result could be an unintended account takeover. At minimum it is a missing authentication check on a state-changing, sensitive operation. Email change is a typical account-takeover step because it enables password reset.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP POST to /settings/email with no session cookie
finding.sink: set_email(g.uid, ...) at routes.py:37, a state-changing account-email update

trace.note: login_optional sets g.uid = session.get('uid'), which is None when there is no session, and never aborts
set_email(g.uid, ...) runs with a None uid for anonymous callers

finding.guards_checked: login_required is applied to /settings/password (line 42) but not here. No other auth check, CSRF protection, or re-authentication was found in the file. Flask session cookie signing only protects a session that exists. set_email at line 48 is a stub, so a None-uid guard inside it is not visible. No before_request hook enforces auth.

verdict.guard_found: none (login_optional at routes.py:19-25 only sets g.uid and never aborts; no before_request hook; set_email at routes.py:48 is a stub with no uid check)
verdict.reason: routes.py:34-37 exposes POST /settings/email with @login_optional (routes.py:22 sets g.uid=None, no abort), so anonymous callers reach set_email(None, ...), unlike /settings/password which uses @login_required (routes.py:42); the sink is a stub so the exact impact depends on the real implementation, but the missing authentication check is real.

verdict_facts.reason: routes.py:35 decorates the state-changing POST /settings/email with @login_optional, which at routes.py:22-23 sets g.uid=None and never aborts, so anonymous callers reach set_email(None, ...) at routes.py:37, while /settings/password at routes.py:42 uses @login_required; set_email at routes.py:48 is a stub with no visible uid guard, so the missing-authentication claim holds, though the account-takeover consequence depends on its unseen implementation.
